Article Title: SC concerned by continuance of derogatory witch-hunting practice
Article Text:
The Supreme Court of India

NEW DELHI: More than 75 years of the Constitution coming into force, the derogatory practice of witch-hunting that targets defenceless women due to prejudice, suspicion, superstition and irrational fear, continues in the country, the Supreme Court lamented while upholding life term for two who murdered a woman in a tribal village of Odisha in Feb 1998.A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and N V Anjaria said the facets of the case had a disturbing impact on the court as a defenceless woman was branded a practitioner of witchcraft and was brutally assaulted in front of her daughter. “What effect it must have had on the daughter of the deceased who had to witness her mother being killed in the most brutal way,” the bench wondered.Writing the judgment, Justice Mishra said the malady of with-hunting continues to plague sections of our society, where prejudice, superstition, and irrational dear supersede the rule of law and constitutional morality.“The brutality associated with witch-hunting extends far beyond the act of killing; where victims mostly women are subjected to torture, beatings, sexual violence and social ostracization. In such a situation, superstitious beliefs or fears are given precedence leading to vulnerable women becoming victims of collective hostility,” he said.IN Feb 1998, in the remote village of tribal inhabited Sundergarh district, one Manobodha Naik’s daughter died, and family members claimed that she died because of witchcraft practice of one Puni Naik.Hearing this Udai Oram dragged Puni Naik to Naik’s house and with his associate, mercilessly assaulted her with sticks leading to her death. The trial court had convicted the duo in 2002, but the Orissa HC took two decades to uphold the conviction and life sentence.Justices Mishra and Anjaria said, “Sometimes in the most difficult situations, it often becomes an easy escape to blame a woman for the acts she did not commit, thus reflecting a deeply rooted social prejudice that often seeks scapegoats rather than solutions. In such situations, what can be given an ascendency is ‘reason’ for reason is the only virtue that stands as a bulwark against collective irrationality.”SC said the Constitution guarantees equality, promotes fraternity and envisages citizens to adopt scientific temperament to rid the society of derogatory practices against women. “Despite this, practices such as witch-hunting continue to persist within a few sections of our society. A Constitutional democracy such as ours cannot survive; wherein such derogatory practices continue to elude the principles of rule of law and Constitutional morality,” it said.
Article Summary: Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and N V Anjaria said the facets of the case had a disturbing impact on the court as a defenceless woman was branded a practitioner of witchcraft. “What effect it must have had on the daughter of the deceased who had to witness her mother being killed in the most brutal way,” the bench wondered.

Article Title: ‘Have to isolate dimaagi Naxals’: PM Modi in Independence Day speech from Red Fort
Article Text:

PM Modi warns against ‘dimagi Naxals’

‘Naxalism is breathing its last’

PM Modi recalls challenges faced by India

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday said armed Naxalism had been curbed but warned that people with Maoist thinking were still present in different parts of the country and needed to be "identified, and isolated".Addressing the nation from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the 80th Independence Day, PM Modi said the country had successfully weakened armed Naxalism but needed to remain alert against what he called "dimagi Naxals"."We need to identify these dimagi naxal, isolate them, and bring the youth together for a developed country," PM Modi said.PM Modi said Naxalism and Maoism had destroyed the aspirations of young people and kept large parts of the country under the grip of violence for decades. He also paid tribute to security personnel who lost their lives fighting the insurgency."Naxalism, Maoism destroyed the dreams of lakhs of youth. It stole the sons of numerous mothers, crushed the dreams of numerous mothers. This naxalism had kept a large part of India and population as a hostage for 4 decades with the barrel of a gun, they had destroyed the Constitution," PM Modi said.He said more than 3,500 security personnel had been killed while protecting citizens from Naxal violence."More than 3,500 security personnel were martyred while protecting the people of the country. More police personnel were killed than soldiers in war, police personnel had to put their lives on the line so that people can get security. This naxalism had covered the country in blood. In 2014, when you gave us the opportunity we had decided that we will rid the country of naxalism, and today I am happy to announce that naxalism does not have even the strength for breathing," the Prime Minister added.PM Modi drew a distinction between armed Naxals and people he described as "dimagi naxal", alleging that the latter continued to look for opportunities to promote violence and push the country in what he called the wrong direction."For years, people with Maoist thinking were there in public life, even in government committees this thinking had affected various institutions and initiatives. My dear countrymen, we have been able to curb and free the country from 'hathariya naxal' (armed naxal). Even if these naxals are gone, but the 'dimagi naxal' (people with naxal thinking), are looking for an opportunity, looking to see ways of violence, and trying to drag the country to a wrong path. We need to identify these dimagi naxal, isolate them, and bring the youth together for a developed country," PM Modi said.PM Modi said areas that were once affected by Naxal violence were now witnessing development, with the Tricolour representing progress and government initiatives flying in regions where armed insurgency had previously held sway."In the 21st century, it is imperative that we eliminate the decades-old challenges that have held the country back. Naxalism and Maoism have destroyed the future of millions of young people. They have snatched away the young sons of countless mothers and shattered the dreams of families across the country. For nearly four decades, Naxalism had held large parts of India and a huge section of its population in its grip, ruling through the barrel of a gun and tearing the Constitution to shreds. More than 3,500 of our police and security personnel sacrificed their lives while protecting ordinary citizens. Naxalism had turned the land red with blood."PM Modi said the government had decided to eliminate Naxalism after coming to power in 2014 and claimed that armed Maoist violence no longer had the strength to sustain itself."When you gave us the opportunity to serve in 2014, we resolved on that very day to free the country from Naxalism.""Today, I am happy to say that Naxalite and Maoist violence no longer has the strength to sustain itself and is breathing its last. We are moving towards completely eliminating it. In areas where the bullets of Naxalites once rang out, where the soil was once stained with blood, today the same Naxal-affected regions are witnessing the tricolour of development, trust and endeavour flying high as they move towards becoming Naxalism-free. "During his Independence Day address, PM Modi also referred to challenges India faced over the past several years, including the Covid-19 pandemic and conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia."In the last 20-12 years, we have faced many dangers. As soon as we emerged from Covid, there was news of wars that started to arise from Ukraine side and West Asia. An atmosphere of tension prevailed. God knows what all the predictions the predictors made!," he said.PM Modi said attempts were also made to create fear among citizens through rumours over the availability of vaccines, petrol, diesel and fertilisers.The remarks formed part of PM Modi's wider Independence Day address, in which he outlined the government's priorities and India's development ambitions as the country moves towards the goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said armed Naxalism had been curbed. He warned that people with Maoist thinking were still present in different parts of the country and needed to be "identified, and isolated" PM Modi paid tribute to security personnel who lost their lives fighting the insurgency.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi , Union ministers and opposition leaders on Saturday extended Independence Day greetings to citizens as India marked its 80th Independence Day, with leaders remembering the freedom struggle while highlighting their visions for the country's future.Prime Minister Modi paid tribute to freedom fighters and said their courage and sacrifice continued to inspire India's journey towards a developed nation.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge , meanwhile, said constitutional values, democratic institutions and social harmony had faced "serious challenges" over the past decade.In a post on X, PM Modi paid tribute to the freedom fighters who fought against colonial rule and said their dreams continued to inspire the country."Warm greetings on the occasion of Independence Day. Article Title: 'This is your last chance': SC ultimatum to Centre over delay in front-of-pack food warning labels
Article Text:
SC gave the government two weeks to take a final call on introducing warning labels for packaged foods.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday sharply criticised the Centre and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India FSSAI ) over the delay in introducing front-of-pack warning labels for packaged food products high in sugar, salt and saturated fat, warning that it would issue directions if the government failed to take a final decision.A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran gave the Centre two weeks to place its final decision on record, making it clear that the government could either implement the proposed warning labels on its own or face judicial intervention."This is your last chance. Next time we will dictate the judgment," the bench said, according to ANI.The court repeatedly underlined that the issue was one of public health, particularly the health of children and questioned the government's reluctance to move ahead with stronger nutritional warnings."Why? You don't want people of this country to remain healthy? More particularly growing children?" the bench asked during the hearing.Appearing for the Centre, additional solicitor general Brijender Chahar argued that applying strict warning standards could create complications for traditional Indian food items. He said products such as namkeen could end up carrying red warning symbols because of their fat or salt content.He also argued that international nutritional standards might not be directly applicable to Indian dietary habits, pointing out that even two eggs could exceed the prescribed daily fat limit.The court, however, was unconvinced.The bench said consumers were already aware that packaged foods contained sugar, fat and carbohydrates, but front-of-pack warning labels would provide a simpler and more effective way of communicating nutritional risks before a purchase was made.The judges also rejected the argument that warning labels could adversely affect manufacturers.According to ANI, the bench observed that the final decision to purchase a product would continue to rest with consumers and that commercial considerations could not take precedence over public health.During the proceedings, senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for a manufacturer, attempted to make submissions. The court responded by stating that the case concerned the health of citizens and that manufacturers could not determine government policy on the issue.Senior advocate Devadutt Kamat suggested that food products could be categorised differently and that detailed nutritional information should be displayed.The bench clarified that it was not opposed to any particular food product but was only seeking greater consumer awareness."In this country, how many people can afford dry fruits? And how many children buy Kurkure? That makes all the difference. We are not against any particular product. We only want the person purchasing it to know what he is consuming," the court said, according to ANI.The bench also referred to its February 10, 2026, order, in which it had previously addressed the issue and laid down its observations.During Thursday's hearing, the petitioner's counsel drew the court's attention to the minutes of an FSSAI meeting held on March 7, which allegedly reflected a position contrary to the suggestions made by the court earlier.The judges also took exception to the Centre's argument that India could not easily adopt international standards relating to nutritional warnings."We do not approve the stance of the Union when it says that it's not possible to match the international standards, more particularly developed countries. Should India remain an undeveloped country?" the bench asked, according to ANI."The world should know that India is concerned about the health of its citizens and more particularly children," it added.The case stems from a petition seeking mandatory front-of-pack warning labels for packaged food products containing high levels of sugar, salt and saturated fat.The proposed labels are intended to help consumers quickly identify potentially unhealthy products before buying them.The issue has also been discussed by Parliament's Committee on Subordinate Legislation, headed by Shiv Sena Rajya Sabha MP Milind Deora, who has advocated studying Singapore's Nutri-Grade model as a possible template for India.Separately, the Union health ministry has proposed displaying "sugar and oil boards" in schools, offices and other public institutions as part of a broader effort to encourage healthier eating habits and reduce excessive consumption of sugar and oil.
Article Summary: Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran gave the Centre two weeks to place its final decision on record. The court repeatedly underlined that the issue was one of public health, particularly the health of children. The proposed labels are intended to help consumers quickly identify potentially unhealthy products.

Article Title: 'Uncalled for': CJI pulls up Bar Council of India over threat of action against NALSAR students

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday expressed “strong disapproval” of the Bar Council of India’s (BCI) now-revoked order barring the enrolment of 2026 graduates of Hyderabad’s NALSAR University of Law as advocates after a section of students objected to the university inviting Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as the chief guest at its convocation ceremony.Kant, heading a bench also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, said students have a right to protest peacefully and described the episode as a “dialogue” between him and the students."If students are protesting peacefully, who is BCI to take action? It is the right of the students to protest peacefully. It is a dialogue between students and me. No one else has to step in," the CJI said.Expressing its strong disapproval, the Supreme Court also stayed any coercive action against students or faculty by BCI or state Councils."It (the letter) was absolutely uncalled for," the bench added.The bench posted the matter for hearing after two weeks.On Thursday, the BCI had directed all state bar councils not to enrol any 2026 graduate of NALSAR University of Law as an advocate until further orders. It withdrew the directive within hours following an uproar on social media.In its initial statement, BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra said the council was examining allegations regarding a campaign against CJI Kant’s participation in the university’s convocation and had sought a report identifying those responsible.The BCI later modified its decision and allowed state bar councils to enrol the university’s 2026 graduates as advocates before withdrawing the notification altogether.The revised notification stated that the “vast majority” of students were innocent and should not be made to suffer for the alleged “misconduct” of a few.Around 450 graduating students of NALSAR had urged the university to reconsider inviting CJI Kant as chief guest, citing his alleged refusal to hear pleas concerning “police brutality” against students who had marched to Parliament on July 20 seeking the resignation of then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG question paper leak in May. Pradhan’s resignation on July 25 brought the protests to an end.
Article Summary: Supreme Court expresses "strong disapproval" of Bar Council of India's now- revoked order. BCI had barred enrolment of 2026 graduates of Hyderabad's NALSAR University of Law as advocates. Students objected to university inviting Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as the chief guest at its convocation ceremony.

Article Title: Phuket plunge: Airbus sends initial report to AI, seeks maintenance details
Article Text:
Airbus has asked Air In- dia to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activi- ties as it continues its event assessment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: “The elevators (control up and down movement of aircraft) and ailerons (controls left and right movement) surfaces were lost for around four seconds.” Airbus, in its initial assessment of the A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi on Aug 4, said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss in altitude that left 24 injured.“Based on analysis of the DFDR (digital flight data recorder),” Airbus found that within seven seconds between 9:32:44 am and 9:32:51 am, there was a loss of hydraulics systems — pressurised fluids which enable flight controls to move. At this point, the autopilot was disconnected and the aircraft’s nose went up (increase in pitch). All timings are in IST.The Airbus preliminary communication sent to AI on Aug 10 says “at (9:32:46 am) auto pilot 2 was disconnected, and full nose down (pitch down) input began being applied on first officer side with no direct response from the flight control surfaces” due to the loss of hydraulics. Five seconds later, a single hydraulic system was recovered and a few seconds later the remaining two systems were back, leading to recovery of normal flight control.Airbus has asked Air India to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activities as it continues its event assessment. “Since load exceedances were detected during the sudden altitude change, (maintenance) inspections must be performed.Please provide the inspection results once they are completed. Please provide more detailed pilot reports from the reported event clarifying what it is observed during the event,” the communication says.“...this event requires an analysis considering both aircraft systems and structural integrity, as airframe may have been affected by the movement,” it adds.While probe is on by Airbus and France’s accident investigator under the ambit of India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau, several pilots are questioning why Air India decided to fly the aircraft all the way to Delhi after it had recovered from the technical events.
Article Summary: Airbus has asked Air India to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activities. Airbus, in its initial assessment of the A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi on Aug 4, said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss in altitude that left 24 injured.

Article Title: Park outside your Bengaluru home? It may soon cost up to Rs 25,000 a year
Article Text:
Bengaluru plans to introduce paid annual permits for on-street residential parking (File photo enhanced with AI)

Rules propose

Private operators to enforce rules

Common parking portal planned

Penalties prescribed

Illegal parking on roads

Rs 500 for cars

Rs 300 for two-wheelers

Parking on footpaths

Rs 1,000 for cars

Rs 600 for two-wheelers

Key conditions

Residential street parking allowed only through permit

Permit valid for one year

Parking outside the permitted area will be treated as a violation





BENGALURU: The city is all set to put a price on one of its most contested public resources, road space.Under the proposed Greater Bengaluru Authority Parking Rules, 2026, residents who want to park their cars on the road outside their homes will have to obtain annual permits, with fees varying by vehicle type.The draft also proposes sweeping restrictions on where vehicles can be parked, particularly around major roads and Metro stations.There are proposals for a complete ban on parking on arterial roads identified as high-density corridors by Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA).It also seeks parking restrictions during peak hours on select arterial roads notified by traffic police.In addition, vehicles would not be allowed to park near junctions, bus stops, transit hubs, pedestrian crossings and footpaths, with detailed setback requirements prescribed under the rules.The proposed rules seek to significantly reduce on-street parking near public transport hubs.Initially, on-street parking would be prohibited within 150 metres of Metro and suburban railway station boundaries. The draft allows city corporations to gradually increase the no-parking zone up to 500 metres.The proposal is expected to impact several high-footfall Metro station areas across the city where commuters currently rely on adjoining roads for parking.In a shift from the current system, the draft proposes to authorise private operators managing public parking facilities to issue violation notices, collect parking-related charges, tow vehicles and clamp vehicles after being formally authorised by city corporations.The operators would be required to record video evidence of violations before towing vehicles, and all towing activities would be overseen by traffic police.To increase organised parking supply, the draft allows city corporations to lease vacant private plots and develop them into public parking facilities.Private landowners who voluntarily convert vacant plots into parking facilities would be eligible for incentives, including property tax exemptions.Owners providing mechanised or multi-level parking facilities could receive 100% exemption from property tax and service charges, while owners offering surface-level parking could receive a 50% exemption.The draft directs Metro, BMTC and suburban rail agencies to create off-street parking facilities on land available with them, particularly at interchange stations and peripheral locations, to encourage park-and-ride travel.Transit agencies may also offer discounted parking rates for commuters using public transport.All parking operators, city corporations and transit agencies would be required to share real-time information on parking availability, occupancy and pricing with GBA.The data would eventually be integrated into a common citywide parking portal and mobile application to help motorists locate available parking spaces and enable authorities to plan future parking infrastructure.Traffic police will continue to have powers to enforce no-parking regulations, tow vehicles and take action against repeat offenders.The draft also allows city corporations to increase parking rates based on demand and location and proposes higher charges for longer parking durations to discourage all-day occupation of valuable road space.

Article Title: CJI, Nalsar students have one query for BCI: ‘Who are you?’

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Friday castigated the Bar Council of India (BCI) for threatening to deny licence to practice to Hyderabad-based NALSAR university students who opposed CJI Surya Kant as their convocation chief guest, shielded them against coercive action, and offered the law graduates a start as legal aid counsel in SC.Taking cognisance of the controversy created late Thursday evening by BCI through an unprecedented letter which had to be hastily retracted, a three-judge bench led by CJI Surya Kant said, “This is absolutely uncalled for. BCI has nothing to do with it. The students might have written a letter to me. It is a dialogue between me and students. Who are they (BCI) to unnecessarily create an issue? This action is totally uncalled for. ”Senior advocate K Parameshwar sought SC’s urgent intervention in quashing the illegal and arbitrary action of the BCI in seeking to coerce VC of NALSAR University, one of the top law schools, to conduct an investigation and identify students who had opposed CJI’s participation in the convocation as chief guest and issuing the now-withdrawn threat that those identified would be denied registration for licence to practice by all state bar councils.Trashing Bar Council of India’s threat to blackball protesting Nalsar students, CJI Surya Kant told senior advocate K Parameshwar to convey to the students, who are completing their graduation in law from Nalsar this year, “to get licences to practice at the earliest and begin their careers in Supreme Court”.The apex court bench sought BCI’s explanation on the process it adopted before passing the resolutions prior to issuing a letter to bar licences to protesters, and another shortly after, retracting it.Urging the students to join the SC bar at the earliest, the CJI said, “We will empanel them and give them legal aid cases. This will be our response to all those who intend to create impediments in their professional career.”He added, “We should be largehearted. Even if someone makes a wrong statement at a young age, let it rest there. That does not mean they do not have a right to speak.”“During my student days, I was actively involved in many student activities. Indulging in activities or protests does not mean the students are wrong. The students have a right to protest peacefully, and no one can stop them. They have a fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression. So long as they are lawfully and peacefully raising their voice over an issue, it must be heard, not opposed. Unnecessarily, Bar Council of India meddled in it.Neither BCI nor any other body has any business to interfere with this,” said the CJI.Earlier, the advocate had raised the now-withdrawn threat that those identified would be denied registration for licence to practise by all state bar councils.The CJI-led bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, without even going through the petition by two formerstudents of Nalsar, restrained BCI and all state bar councils from taking any coercive or punitive action against the students and faculty.Accepting the notice on behalf of BCI, advocate Radhika Gautam said the objectionable circular had been withdrawn. In its order, the Supreme Court asked Bar Council of India to file its counter-affidavit in two weeks.
Article Summary: Bar Council of India (BCI) threatened to deny licence to practice to Hyderabad- based NALSAR university students who opposed CJI Surya Kant as their convocation chief guest. The apex court bench sought BCI’s explanation on the process it adopted before passing the resolutions.

Article Title: Cockroaches, expired food: Maharashtra FDA suspends 14 licences linked to Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licences of 14 food business establishments linked to quick-commerce platforms Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart after a statewide inspection drive uncovered multiple food safety and hygiene violations.The August 13 drive covered 86 establishments across Maharashtra involved in the storage, sale and delivery of food through online platforms. The FDA issued 60 improvement notices and ordered one facility to temporarily halt operations, news agency PTI reported.Of the 14 suspended licences, five were linked to Blinkit, five to Zepto, two to Instamart, while one each belonged to Bhagwati Stores and Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd.The inspections focused on storage conditions, temperature control, cleanliness, pest management, personal hygiene of food handlers, food safety records, display of licences and compliance with inventory practices such as First In, First Out (FIFO) and First Expired, First Out (FEFO).In Pune, the FDA suspended the licence of a Zepto outlet in Lohegaon after inspectors found food items stored beyond their declared "use by" dates.The regulator also flagged unhygienic storage conditions, inadequate pest control and lapses in personal hygiene, adding that the company's response during the hearing was unsatisfactory.Another Pune facility operated by Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd was found to have a cockroach infestation, inadequate cold-chain maintenance for frozen products and deficiencies in hygiene and pest-control practices.In Mumbai, a Blinkit facility in Malad (West) was found to be operating with chiller temperatures above the prescribed limit. Inspectors also found that around 40 food handlers had not undergone mandatory medical examinations and that records were unavailable.The FDA said several workers were not using protective gear such as gloves, aprons and head coverings. Inspectors also found damaged storage racks, poor organisation and inadequate segregation of different categories of food products.At another Blinkit facility in Ghatkopar, officials flagged shortcomings in drainage, waste disposal, temperature control and housekeeping. The outlet was classified as non-compliant after scoring 46 per cent during the inspection.Inspections at Zepto facilities in Mulund and Goregaon revealed deficiencies related to food storage, temperature management, cleanliness and licence display.At an Instamart outlet in Andheri, inspectors found food packets stored directly on the floor. The FDA also reported inadequate storage space, overcrowding and deficiencies in hygiene and temperature control.The inspection drive also covered delivery operations.At a Blinkit store in Karad in Satara district, officials checked 125 delivery riders and found that they lacked identity cards and medical fitness records. The regulator also found that the outlet's FSSAI licence was not displayed on delivery bags and boxes.The FDA directed the company to suspend two-wheeler delivery operations at the outlet until the deficiencies were addressed.The regulator said the action was taken under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and urged all food businesses operating through online platforms to strictly comply with prescribed food safety, hygiene and storage standards.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licences of 14 food business establishments linked to quick-commerce platforms Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart. Inspections uncovered violations ranging from cockroach infestation and expired food to poor hygiene and storage practices.

Article Title: 40 queries in Census Phase-II: Caste, bank accounts, Covid jabs...
Article Text:
Data will remain confidential, can’t be used for legal evidence, govt benefits or public disclosure

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The second phase of Census 2027 — involving population enumeration, will, for the first time, capture caste “as declared by the respondent” among its 40 fields, which include new ones such as number of bank accounts, place of Covid vaccination and voter card number.Enumeration by caste will not delve into the question of whether it falls under other backward classes (OBC) category. However, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes will be enumerated as earlier, with all notified SC/ST communities listed in the drop-down menus.In a first, the questionnaire notified Friday for the upcoming population enumeration phase of Census 2027, shall seek the name of the spouse, parents’ particulars and nationality — elements captured by the national population register ( exercise undertaken alongside Census 2011 and proposed to be repeated with Census 2021 before the latter was postponed due to Covid. NPR updation was however delinked from Census 2027.The Phase 2 questionnaire lists 40 questions, up from 29 asked during Census 2011. The new fields include, apart from caste, spouse’s name and mother and father’s particulars, the respondent’s nationality as declared, permanent address, place of Covid-19 vaccination, total number of bank accounts, mobile number, Aadhaar number, voter ID number, passport number and availability of driving license.While the mobile number, Aadhaar no and voter ID may be shared if available, the passport number is required only from an Indian passport holder.Sources told TOI that mother and father’s particulars are likely to capture their names, date of birth and place of birth. While these are key factors that determine citizenship/nationality, their capture will have no impact on individuals since individual census data must remain confidential and cannot be used for “legal evidence, govt benefits or public disclosure,” as per the govt. A senior govt functionary said the aggregate data, however, may give a picture of overall population that meets the citizenship criteria as per the Citizenship Act.TOI was the first to report on August 3 that the Phase 2 questionnaire shall capture caste “as declared by the respondent” and, in a first, also capture parents’ date and place of birth.Sources said that giving the drop down option for enumeration was not found to be feasible because states have different classes categorised as OBCs, with mismatch between the communities recognised as such by the Centre and those at the level of states. Sources also pointed to the trend of states expanding their respective OBC lists by adding more castes/classes, something which could have created logistical problems once the Census was underway.Officials told TOI that unlike the socio-economic caste census conducted in 2011 — which had returned around 46 lakh castes, making it unusable — the digital mode of Census 2027 and availability of modern, AI-based tools can surmount compilation and segregation challenges. Also, the full confidentiality of an individual’s caste declaration is guaranteed by the Census Act.In other shifts from previous census exercises, the fertility data to be collected in Census 2027 will skip the differentiation between male and female children. Also, literacy status will separately capture digital literacy.Even though an individual’s aadhaar no, voter ID and passport details enumerated as part of census cannot be disclosed to any entity, including govt departments, sources said the data, when aggregated, can give the big picture on coverage of these documents and identify the gaps. Similarly, the number of bank accounts will give an idea of the penetration and distribution of banking services.Phase 2 is due to start in Union territory of Ladakh and the snow-bound, non-synchronous areas of J&K, Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh on August 17; self-enumeration window will run from August 17 to 31, followed by field enumeration from Sept 1 to 30. For the rest of the country, the population enumeration will resume in February 2027, culminating in the population headcount with March 1, 2027, as the reference date.Phase 1 of Census is due to be completed across the country by Sept 30, 2026.Among the usual fields included in the Phase 2 questionnaire are religion, age at marriage, disability, mother tongue and other spoken languages, education, occupation and migration.
Article Summary: The Phase 2 questionnaire lists 40 questions, up from 29 asked during Census 2011. The new fields include, apart from caste, spouse’s name and mother and father's particulars. Data will remain confidential, can’t be used for legal evidence, govt benefits or public disclosure.

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh (BMS) has called for nationwide protests on August 17 over a range of pending labour issues, including higher minimum pension, revision of EPF and ESI wage ceilings, restoration of the Old Pension Scheme and changes to provisions of the new labour codes.The organisation has asked all its units across the country to hold demonstrations, rallies and dharnas at district headquarters and submit memorandums to the Prime Minister, finance minister and labour minister. A major protest is planned at Jantar Mantar in Delhi from 10am, with workers and representatives of BMS-affiliated unions and federations expected to participate.Among its key demands, BMS has sought an increase in the minimum pension under EPS-95 to Rs 7,500 a month and its linkage with variable dearness allowance and Ayushman Bharat. It has also demanded that the ESI wage ceiling be doubled from Rs 21,000 to Rs 42,000 and the EPF ceiling raised from Rs 15,000 to Rs 30,000.The union has sought bonus on full wages in line with the new labour codes, an increase in the wage ceiling used for bonus calculation and gratuity based on 30 days' wages instead of 15 days, without any upper limit. It has also demanded inflation-linked minimum wages, higher honorarium for anganwadi, ASHA, mid-day meal and other scheme workers, and equal pay for contract and outsourced workers doing the same work.Other demands include a five-day work week in banks, filling vacancies in government services and public establishments, convening the Indian Labour Conference and restoring OPS.BMS has also reiterated its opposition to several provisions of the Industrial Relations Code and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, arguing that they could weaken workers' rights, job security and social security. It has sought formal consultations between the Centre and central trade unions before amendments are made.The organisation also wants the Centre and states to reconsider the status of more than one crore “scheme workers”, saying many work 10-12 hours a day but remain outside effective labour-law and social-security protection.

Article Title: Govt scraps 12-minute ad cap for TV channel
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Television channels will no longer be restricted to 12 minutes of advertisements per hour, with the government deciding to scrap the two-decade-old cap in a move it says will put traditional broadcasters on a more level footing with digital platforms.The restriction, introduced in 2006 under the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994, will cease to apply once the amended rules are notified in the Gazette, the information and broadcasting ministry said.The government has argued that the television landscape has changed substantially since the cap was imposed. India had only 62 TV channels in 2006, compared with more than 900 now. Cable television, then the dominant distribution platform, was largely analog and offered limited capacity and consumer choice.With digitisation, platforms including cable TV, direct-to-home, HITS and IPTV can now carry 300 to 500 channels or more, significantly expanding viewer choice and competition, the ministry said.The decision could give broadcasters greater flexibility to determine advertising inventory, an important consideration for an industry that remains heavily dependent on advertising revenue across both pay and free-to-air channels.The ministry also cited the growing competition television faces from digital media, where there is no comparable statutory cap on advertising duration.It said the existing restriction had created a “non-level playing field” for conventional television broadcasters and that removing it would promote “fair competition” and ease of doing business.The change, however, will become operational only from the date the amendment to the Cable Television Networks Rules is formally notified.
Article Summary: The restriction, introduced in 2006 under the Cable Television Networks Rules, 1994, will cease to apply once the amended rules are notified in the Gazette. Article Title: Pew survey: What US, UK and others think about India at 80
Article Text:
At 80, India is increasingly a country the world has an opinion about.

Read more:

Neighbourhood contrasts & global scorecard

as India enters its 80th year as an independent nation, what does the world think of it?

India's image is changing

Politics matters too

A mixed but largely positive global image

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

As India completes 79 years of independence, its global standing presents a striking study in contrasts.A Pew Research Center survey conducted across 36 countries between February and May 2026 reveals an international community divided down the middle: a global median of 45% of respondents hold a favorable view of India, while 41% express an unfavorable opinion.Behind this median lies a complex tapestry of geopolitical shifts, historical rivalries, and evolving regional alliances.From enthusiasm in Western Europe and East Africa to frosty hostility in parts of the Middle East and South Asia, public perception of the world’s most populous democracy depends heavily on where you ask.Nowhere is this divergence more intense than in India's immediate backyard. While proximity can foster cooperation, in South Asia it has produced antithetical attitudes.Sri Lanka has the most favourable view of India, with 79% of adults expressing a positive opinion.Pakistan sits at the opposite end, with just 7% viewing India favourably. The gulf between the two countries reflects decades of conflict, political rivalry and competing national narratives.Turkey is another major outlier. Only 15% of Turks have a favourable opinion of India, while a majority hold an unfavourable view.In the West Bank and East Jerusalem, just 18% express a positive opinion.Yet beyond these pockets of hostility, India finds considerable goodwill across much of the world.Kenya and the United Kingdom rank alongside Sri Lanka among the countries most positive towards India, with roughly seven in 10 adults expressing favourable views.Majorities in Germany, Israel, Italy, Sweden, Japan and Thailand also see India positively.In contrast, Latin American publics express mixed-to-negative views, alongside substantial shares of respondents who offer no opinion.The findings suggest that India's global image is not simply a reflection of its diplomatic alliances.Economic ties, strategic partnerships, cultural familiarity and perceptions of India's growing global role all appear to shape how people view the country.The bigger story is perhaps not where India stands today, but how its image has changed.In most countries surveyed, opinions have remained relatively stable since Pew last asked the question. But in 10 countries, the change has been statistically significant — and in seven of them, India's favourability has fallen.Turkey and Nigeria have recorded the sharpest declines since 2025, with the share of people expressing a favourable opinion of India falling by 10 percentage points in both countries.India has also lost ground in the United States, Indonesia, South Africa and Mexico.The decline is particularly striking in Bangladesh.Pew's previous survey there was conducted in 2024. Since then, the share of Bangladeshis with a favourable opinion of India has fallen by 15 percentage points, leaving fewer than half with a positive view.At the same time, the number of Bangladeshis who do not express an opinion has also fallen sharply, from 24% to just 7%. In other words, more Bangladeshis now appear to have a defined opinion of India — and that opinion has become considerably less favourable.The trend is not uniformly negative, however.India's image has improved significantly in Germany, Britain and Sri Lanka.The share of Britons with a favourable opinion of India has risen 11 points since 2025, while Germany has recorded a six-point increase. Sri Lanka has seen an even bigger jump, with favourability rising 14 points since 2024.Looking further back to 2023 reveals another interesting divide.Across several European countries, India's image has strengthened substantially since the first post-pandemic survey. In Germany, for example, only 47% had a favourable opinion of India in 2023. That figure has now climbed to 63%.France has followed a similar trajectory. India's favourability there has risen from 39% in 2023 to 50% today.Outside Europe, however, the picture is less encouraging.South Korea is one example. In 2023, 59% of South Koreans viewed India favourably. Today, that figure has dropped to 44%.Latin America also tends to lean more negative, although large numbers of people in several European and Latin American countries do not express an opinion at all.India's global image is also shaped by domestic political ideology in some countries.The United States and Canada show a striking pattern: people on the political left are more likely than conservatives to view India favourably.In the US, 54% of liberals express a positive opinion of India, compared with 40% of conservatives. In Canada, the corresponding figures are 58% and 45%.Israel presents almost the exact opposite picture.There, 68% of people on the political right view India favourably, compared with just 46% on the left.The ideological divide underlines how perceptions of India can be tied not only to India's own policies, but also to how different political constituencies interpret its role in the world.So, as India enters its 80th year as an independent nation, what does the world think of it?The answer is neither uniformly celebratory nor overwhelmingly negative.Pakistan and Turkey may give India the stink eye, but they represent the more hostile end of a much broader spectrum.From Sri Lanka and Kenya to Britain, Germany and Israel, India enjoys strong positive sentiment in several strategically important countries.At the same time, the declines in Bangladesh, the US, South Korea, Turkey, Nigeria and other countries show that India's global image cannot be taken for granted.India's international reputation is therefore becoming more consequential — and more contested.As New Delhi seeks a larger role in global affairs, its challenge will not simply be to build economic and military power, but also to shape how that power is perceived abroad.At 80, India is increasingly a country the world has an opinion about.
Article Summary: A Pew Research Center survey conducted across 36 countries between February and May 2026 reveals an international community divided down the middle. A global median of 45% of respondents hold a favorable view of India, while 41% express an unfavorable opinion. In 10 countries, the change has been statistically significant — and in seven of them, India's favourability has fallen.

NEW DELHI: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Friday said India's defence sector had undergone an “unprecedented transformation” over the past 12 years, with domestic defence production rising nearly fourfold to a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26.In his message to soldiers on the eve of Independence Day, Rajnath said India had reduced its dependence on defence imports while strengthening indigenous manufacturing under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India initiatives.""You all know that under the leadership of the Hon'ble Prime Minister, our government has always accorded the highest priority to self-reliance in the defence sector. Over the past 12 years, you have witnessed unprecedented transformation in the defence sector through Aatmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India," he said.“Our domestic defence production, which stood at around Rs 46,000 crore in 2014, reached a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025-26. This means that over the past decade, our domestic defence production has increased nearly fourfold. This is proof of the structural changes that have taken place over the past decade," the defence minister added.The union minister further highlighted recent tests and developments in indigenous defence technology, including the MIRV-equipped Advanced Agni missile, Rudram-II air-to-surface missile, Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile and Pinaka Long Range Guided Rocket.“We have also made major advances in hypersonic technology. The successful demonstration of Solid Fuel Ducted Ramjet technology is equally significant,” he said.He also said the first successful test of the indigenous Kusha Long Range Surface-to-Air Missile had strengthened India's air-defence capabilities.As Rajnath hailed the growth in defence sector, the ministry of defence said India's defence production reached a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26, nearly four times the level of 2014. The government said defence exports have grown 56-fold, from Rs 686 crore in 2013-14 to Rs 38,424 crore in 2025-26, with Indian defence products now reaching more than 80 countries.The defence budget has increased 3.1-fold, from Rs 2.53 lakh crore in 2013-14 to Rs 7.85 lakh crore in 2026-27, while capital expenditure has risen 2.3-fold to Rs 2.19 lakh crore. Defence R&D spending has more than doubled to Rs 29,100 crore in 2026-27 from Rs 13,716 crore in 2014-15.The ministry said the Indian Army has achieved roughly 91% self-sufficiency in ammunition, having indigenised 159 of 175 ammunition variants.The government is targeting Rs 3 lakh crore in annual defence production and Rs 50,000 crore in defence exports by 2029.
Article Summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh says India's defence sector has undergone an ‘unprecedented transformation’ over the past 12 years. Domestic defence production has risen nearly fourfold to a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore in 2025-26.

Article Title: 'First time we did something like this': Former women Naxalites share their Raipur ramp-walk experience

Surrendered women naxals walk on the ramp during a participation in a Tribal fashion show programme.

NEW DELHI: For nine women from Chhattisgarh's Naxal-affected Bastar region, the stage in Raipur offered a strikingly different kind of experience. Once part of an armed insurgency, they recently walked the ramp in handloom outfits at a National Handloom Day event, as part of efforts to help surrendered Naxalites rebuild their lives.The women, all from Sukma, took part in a Swadeshi fashion show organised as part of rehabilitation efforts for former Naxalites.Sukma SP Mayank Gurjar said the event also gave them an opportunity to promote Swadeshi products.For some of the women, the experience was unlike anything they had done before. One former Naxalite, who had worked with the Pamed Area Committee, said she surrendered in 2026 and travelled to Raipur for six days of training before taking part in the programme."I used to work in the Pamed Area Committee. I surrendered in 2026. We went to Raipur recently. There, we were trained by people who had come from Bombay...prominent ministers also came. The training was of six days...it was the first time we did something like that...we enjoyed it," the former Naxalite told news agency ANI.Another participant, Poonam Devi, said her journey with the Naxalite movement had begun in November 2007.She surrendered on July 12, 2025, bringing that chapter of her life to an end."I surrendered on July 12, 2025. I liked the program...we were trained for it...I joined the Naxals in November 2007 and left in 2025," she said.According to Gurjar, the women's participation reflects the opportunities being offered under the rehabilitation policies of the Central and Chhattisgarh governments to those who surrender and choose to return to mainstream society."As you all know, through the rehabilitation policy of the Government of India and the Chhattisgarh Government, various benefits and advantages are being provided to surrendered Naxalites. In that context, on National Handloom Day, nine surrendered women who had surrendered in Sukma participated in a Swadeshi fashion show," he said.The nine women had held different positions within the Naxalite organisation. Some were associated with the Pamed Area Committee, while others had served as gunners for senior Naxalite commanders in Battalion Number 1. One had worked as a school teacher within the organisation, according to the SP."Among the nine surrendered women, some were working in the Pamed Area Committee. Some worked as gunners for major Naxalite commanders in Battalion Number 1. One of the surrendered women Naxalites was working as a teacher in a school," Gurjar said.Their past also included handling weapons. Gurjar said one of the women had carried an INSAS rifle and that the participants had surrendered around six months earlier.Now, instead of carrying weapons, the women are being encouraged to explore skills and opportunities that can help them build a different future.Gurjar said their participation in the fashion show showed a change in their outlook and suggested that their confidence in the rehabilitation process was growing."They are now actively promoting Swadeshi products and refining their artistic skills," he said.For women who once lived amid the forests and violence of the Naxal movement, walking a ramp in handloom clothing may appear like a small moment. But within the larger rehabilitation effort, it represents something much more significant, a visible step away from an armed past and towards an ordinary life.
Article Summary: Nine women from Chhattisgarh's Naxal-affected Bastar region took part in a Swadeshi fashion show. The event was organised as part of rehabilitation efforts for former Noxalites. The women are being encouraged to explore skills that can help them build a different future.

NEW DELHI: The Joint Action Forum on Minorities that had led a delegation of representatives of Churches to meet Home Minister Amit Shah last week described the decision of the govt to refer the FCRA Amendment Bill 2026 to a Joint Parliamentary Committee as a “positive step” that presents an “important opportunity for a comprehensive, clause-by-clause review of its provisions and their implications”.A host of Church bodies last week met and urged home minister Amit Shah to either withdraw the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill or send it to a joint parliamentary committee for scrutiny.In their representation to HM, the delegation representing Catholic, Protestant and Orthodox Churches from across India organised under Joint Action Forum on Minorities with DMK MP P Wilson as its chairperson, had sought that the Bill is withdrawn in entirety or in alternate be referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee together with a review of the working of the Principal FCRA Act 2010 itself".On Wednesday, Wilson in a statement on X thanked DMK President MK Stalin and all opposition parties in the Lok Sabha for their unified demand to withdraw the FCRA Amendment Bill 2026, even though it was decided by a majority voice vote to refer it to the Joint Parliamentary Committee.“Although the govt has not agreed to withdraw the FCRA Bill 2026 entirely, the Union Government's decision to refer the Bill to the Joint Parliamentary Committee is a positive step,” he added.“This is a sensitive issue where a balance must be struck between the govt’s authority over financial control and the rights of minority institutions to receive charitable contributions. NEW DELHI: The Congress spent a total Rs 248.6 crore on its campaign for the recent assembly elections in Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry, even as its total receipts between the date of announcement and completion of these polls stood at Rs 207.1 crore.According to Congress's election expenditure statement for the five state/UT polls, filed on July 31 with the Election Commission, the party received Rs 104 crore in cash and Rs 103.1 crore via cheque or draft between March 15, 2026, when the elections were announced, and May 6, 2026, when they had concluded.The Congress's full poll expense statement shows its total opening balance of cash in hand (including at the level of its central headquarters and the state/district/local level units of the 5 states/UTs) at Rs 22.9 crore and its cash in bank at Rs 146.1 crore. At the end of the polls, its cash in hand was marginally lower at Rs 22.6 crore while its bank balance had declined by 45% to Rs 80.6 crore.On the expenditure side, the party declared a total spend of Rs 143 crore on general party propaganda and Rs 105.6 crore on candidates. The latter includes Rs 95.5 crore given by the party as lump-sum payments to its candidates across the five poll-gone states/UT; while the central party headquarters bore Rs 95.3 crore of expenditure under this head, the state/district/local units disbursed only Rs 23 lakh among the candidates.Expenses on virtual campaigns through social media platforms and applications were declared at Rs 6.8 crore.Over Rs 3.2 crore was spent by the Congress on publicising the criminal antecedents of its candidates.As part of general party propaganda, the Congress spent Rs 92.5 crore on media advertisements, covering print and electronic space, bulk SMS, cable TV, websites and TV channels. Another Rs 8 crore funded public meetings, processions and rallies, while Rs 11.5 crore was spent on badges, posters, cutouts, hoardings etc and nearly Rs 2 crore on miscellaneous propaganda items.Poll surveys and campaigns for the five assembly elections cost the Congress Rs 4.8 crore.A total Rs 23.5 crore was spent by the grand old party on the travel and lodging of its star campaigners (Rs 21.8 crore) and other leaders. The aircraft and helicopters were sourced from Air Charter Services Pvt Ltd, Aircab Aviation, A R Airways, GMP Air Charter, Lima Tang Aviation Service, Devigo Data Systems and Global Vectra.The Congress's central headquarters routed Rs 83.2 crore of its lump-sum payments to candidates through the state/UT units; with Kerala unit getting the largest share at Rs 55.1 crore, followed by Puducherry (Rs 10 crore), West Bengal (Rs 9 crore), Tamil Nadu (Rs 7.1 crore) and Assam (Rs 2 crore).The Congress-led UDF seized power in Kerala, but the party or its alliances performed poorly in other states, managing 21 seats in Assam, 6 in Puducherry and 2 in West Bengal, while drawing a blank in Tamil Nadu.
Article Summary: The Congress spent a total Rs 248.6 crore on its campaign for the recent assembly elections. The party received Rs 104 crore in cash and Rs 103.1 crore via cheque or draft. As part of general party propaganda, the Congress spent Rs 92.5 crore on media advertisements.

NEW DELHI: DMK on Wednesday supported the Tamil Nadu government’s resolution opposing the Centre’s proposed delimitation exercise, with Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin saying the state’s representation in the Lok Sabha should not be reduced.He said the number of Members of Parliament from Tamil Nadu should not be reduced in the name of delimitation and called for the exercise to be deferred for 25 years."In the name of constituency delimitation, the number of Members of Parliament should not be reduced. Our stand is that constituency delimitation should not be carried out for the next 25 years. We welcome the resolution on the 33% reservation for women. Our firm stand is that Tamil Nadu should not be affected by constituency delimitation. The movement that first told India what the impact of delimitation would be is the DMK," Udhayanidhi added.The development comes after Tamil Nadu assembly on Wednesday passed a resolution in the state Assembly opposing the Union government’s proposed delimitation exercise.Speaking in the assembly, CM Vijay also called for the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections based on the existing 543 constituencies."The 33% reservation for women should be implemented in the 2029 Lok Sabha elections itself, based on the existing 543 constituencies. The 33% reservation for women should not be delayed any further. In Tamil Nadu, more women have voted than men. Providing reservation for women is not a concession; it is a matter of social justice. The 33% reservation for women must be implemented without any further delay," he said.The resolution seeks to safeguard the political representation of southern states, particularly Tamil Nadu, arguing that their success in controlling population growth should not result in reduced representation in Parliament."All the states including Tamil Nadu and the people / elected representatives of the union territories have not had their population counted for more than 50 years. The next census to count the population was supposed to be held in 2026. Therefore, since the delimitation of constituencies has not been carried out for the last 50 years, based on the 2011 population census, the constituencies should be delimited and the number of Lok Sabha and Assembly members should be increased from 550 to 850 by bringing in a constitutional amendment Bill," the resolution stated.The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, was introduced in the Lok Sabha on April 16, proposing to increase the strength of the Lower House to 850 seats and expedite the implementation of the Women's Reservation Bill passed in 2023. However, the Bill failed to secure the constitutionally required two-thirds majority of members present and voting and was not passed.While the Congress and other opposition parties have supported the Women's Reservation Bill, they have opposed the proposed delimitation exercise and called for an increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats. Article Title: 5 indigenous small modular reactors targeted by 2033, Jitendra Singh tells LS
Article Text:
Union MoS Jitendra Singh speaks in the Lok Sabha during the Monsoon session of Parliament

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A key objective of the govt under the Nuclear Energy Mission is to develop and operationalise at least five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033, minister for department of atomic energy Jitendra Singh said in a written reply in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is undertaking the design and development of indigenous SMR technologies, including the 220 MWe Bharat Small Modular Reactor (BSMR-200) and 55 MWe SMR-55 for power generation. BARC is also developing a high temperature gas cooled reactor (HTGCR) of up to 5 MW capacity, which can be coupled with a suitable thermochemical cycle for hydrogen production.Singh said India is steadily strengthening its indigenous nuclear energy ecosystem with a focus on advanced reactor technologies, SMRs, domestic manufacturing capabilities, private-sector participation and long-term utilisation of the country’s abundant thorium resources. The govt has adopted a two-pronged approach to accelerate nuclear capacity addition. This includes deployment of large indigenous reactors such as 700 MWe pressurised heavy water reactors (PHWRs) and advanced reactor designs at greenfield sites, alongside development and deployment of SMRs at brownfield locations, including retiring fossil-fuel-based power plants, captive plants for energy-intensive industries and off-grid applications in remote areas.The minister also highlighted continuing work of the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) in advancing the second stage of India’s nuclear power programme. IGCAR is pursuing multidisciplinary scientific research and advanced engineering development for sodium cooled fast breeder reactors and associated closed fuel-cycle facilities, technologies that remain a cornerstone of India’s long-term nuclear strategy.On thorium, Singh said India is pursuing its three-stage nuclear power programme, based on a closed fuel cycle, to optimise utilisation of its uranium resources and progressively harness its abundant thorium reserves. Thorium, being a fertile material, needs to be converted into fissile uranium-233 in a nuclear reactor before it can be used for energy generation.India has already undertaken sustained R&D towards thorium utilisation. Thorium Oxide (Thoria) pellets have been used in the initial cores of operating PHWRs, while Thoria-based fuels have also been irradiated in BARC research reactors. The irradiated Thoria pins have been reprocessed to obtain uranium-233, which has subsequently been fabricated as fuel for the KAMINI reactor at IGCAR, Kalpakkam. Singh said the Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, 2025 has been enacted to enable wider participation of both public and private entities in the nuclear sector.
Article Summary: The govt under the Nuclear Energy Mission is to develop and operationalise at least five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033. Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is undertaking the design and development of indigenous SMR technologies. The govt has adopted a two-pronged approach to accelerate nuclear capacity addition.

Article Title: Supreme Court pushes 19 states, union territories to notify cancer
Article Text:
Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With the National Cancer Registry Programme covering only a fraction of India’s population and rural cancer surveillance remaining particularly limited, the Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting. The court on Tuesday asked the 19 States and Union Territories that have not yet notified cancer as a notifiable disease to consider doing so, a move that could make reporting of newly detected cases to public health authorities mandatory.Such notification could help plug gaps in cancer surveillance by giving health authorities a more complete picture of the country’s cancer burden, including where cases are rising and which populations are most affected. The data could in turn help shape policies on prevention, early detection, treatment capacity and allocation of healthcare resources.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant passed the order on a plea filed by a retired AIIMS doctor after his lawyer Gaurav Bansal told the court that NCRP covers only 10% of population and rural coverage is less than 1%.The push assumes greater significance against the backdrop of the WHO’s latest Global Status Report on Cancer, which estimates that 92% of people globally will be affected by cancer either directly or through a close family member.The report also projects annual cancer cases to rise to nearly 35 million by 2050.The Supreme Court was informed that 17 of India’s 36 States and UTs have already notified cancer, following recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare. The remaining 19 have now been asked to consider similar action.Dr Pragya Shukla, Head of Clinical Oncology at Delhi State Cancer Institute, said standardised, disease-specific and timely data was essential to track India's changing cancer burden, identify regional and demographic trends, and assess the impact of prevention and treatment programmes. Such a system, she said, would complement existing cancer registries, help identify high-burden areas, improve planning for treatment infrastructure and medicines, and strengthen evidence-based cancer control. Govil added that reliable data would be critical for planning prevention, early detection and resource allocation.The Indian Cancer Society welcomed the intervention, saying national notification could help build a comprehensive cancer surveillance system. “The Supreme Court’s intervention is a significant development, and we welcome its direction to the remaining States and Union Territories to move towards cancer notification,” said Jyotsna Govil, Chairperson, Indian Cancer Society, Delhi. However, she stressed that notification alone would not suffice and called for a uniform national framework with common definitions, reporting standards and data protocols to ensure comparable and interoperable data across states.
Article Summary: Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting. The court on Tuesday asked the 19 States and Union Territories that have not yet notified cancer as a notifiable disease to consider doing so. The move could make reporting of newly detected cases to public health authorities mandatory.

ALWAR: A heated confrontation broke out between Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka and Thanagazi SHO Mahavir Singh during a protest by school students in Jodhwas village of Rajasthan's Alwar district on Friday, with Ranka invoking the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan after the party's Jantar Mantar protest.Ranka had reached Jodhwas to join students protesting the condition of their government school, where a slab from a dilapidated building had collapsed two days ago.During the confrontation with the SHO, Ranka said that the country's education minister had been removed following the protest, and asserted that the interests of students in Rajasthan would not be allowed to be compromised."Mere sath politics mat khelna. Desh ke shiksha mantri ko hata ke aaye hain (don't play politics with us. During the altercation, a young man's shirt was torn. Ranka demanded that those responsible for tearing the shirt be identified and immediate action be taken against them.He also pressed the administration to accept the students' demands without delay.What triggered the students' protest?The students of Government Senior Secondary School in Jodhwas had been protesting for the second consecutive day after a slab from the roof of the school's dilapidated building suddenly collapsed on Wednesday.No student was injured in the incident, but the collapse renewed concerns over the safety of the school building.The students have been demanding that the unsafe structure be demolished, repairs be carried out and the shortage of teachers be addressed.The school's four-room old building had been declared dilapidated last year and has remained shut since then. The school is currently functioning with only three rooms, some of which are being used as the staff room and principal's room. Students have also complained that these rooms leak during the rainy season.Ranka warns of bigger agitationSpeaking during the protest, Ranka warned that the CJP would launch what he described as the biggest agitation in Rajasthan since Independence if dilapidated school buildings were not repaired within three months.He claimed that 84,000 classrooms across Rajasthan were in a dilapidated condition, putting the future of more than 15 lakh children at risk.Ranka also questioned the state's funding for school infrastructure, saying that state education minister Madan Dilawar had stated that around Rs 20,000 crore would be required to construct the buildings, while the government had released only Rs 500 crore.He demanded that the government arrange funds from wherever necessary, including the PM CARES Fund or other sources, or seek funds or loans from the Centre to ensure that school buildings were constructed quickly."We cannot allow children to die in such dilapidated buildings," Ranka said, according to the statement provided.Administration accepts students' demandsAfter Ranka's intervention, talks were held between the students and the administration. The protest ended on Friday evening after officials agreed to the students' demands.These included demolition of the dilapidated building, early appointment of teachers, starting construction of a new school building within three months, repair of the damaged bridge on the approach road, repair of six existing classrooms within a week and allocation of a playground.District education officer Manoj Sharma said the shortage of teachers would be addressed and efforts would be made to get posts for lecturers and second-grade teachers sanctioned.Thanagazi development officer Vikas Kumar also confirmed that the administration had accepted the students' five major demands, including demolition of the unsafe structure, teacher appointments, construction of a new building, repair of the bridge, classroom repairs and allocation of a playground.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka and Thanagazi SHO Mahavir Singh had a heated confrontation during a protest.
